You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected User Input: I need a channel beam with 70mm width, 40mm height, a length 450mm with a wall thickness of 5mm, which is open on the top side | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

To create the channel beam, we will use the `block` function twice.

First, a solid block will be created with the outer dimensions of the beam: 70mm width (x-size), 40mm height (y-size), and 450mm length (z-size). This block will be the base of our geometry, so the `subtraction` parameter will be set to `False`.

Second, another block will be created to hollow out the channel. This block will be subtracted from the first one. Its dimensions will be calculated to leave a 5mm wall thickness.
- The width (x-size) will be 60mm (70mm - 2 * 5mm).
- The height (y-size) will be 35mm (40mm - 5mm), as the channel is open on top.
- The length (z-size) will be the same, 450mm.
This subtraction block will be positioned at (x=5, y=5, z=0) to create the desired wall thickness on the sides and bottom. For this block, the `subtraction` parameter will be set to `True`.

This two-step process of creation and subtraction will result in the requested C-channel beam.
